title: Stop the Archive check and change pr from telling a copy already archived upstream to run ship
description: Stop the Archive check and change pr from telling a copy already archived upstream to run ship
acceptance_criteria: With the remote default holding an archive of a change that this branch still holds unarchived, the pull-request sentence printed by `change status` and `change pr` names `specsync change status <id>`, never `specsync change ship <id>`, even when the stale copy carries a passing review whose `implementation_commit` equals `HEAD` and a verification record.

`.github/scripts/archive-readiness.sh` reaches the same verdict and prints the same sentence when the remote default ref is present (`origin/HEAD`, else `origin/main`, else `origin/master`), using the same test as `upstream_archive_of`: a dated package of this change id on that ref whose `state.json` carries the id, added by a commit `HEAD` does not contain.

An archive `HEAD` already contains (the reopen-and-rearchive path) and a repository with no remote default ref keep today's classification; the script never fetches, so the Archive job's single-commit checkout cannot see upstream archives, and that job still fails on any open change.
A copy with no upstream archive and a passing review at `HEAD` is still told `specsync change ship <id>` by both.
A Rust test (`an_upstream_archived_copy_is_not_told_to_ship` in `commands::change`) and a `test-archive-readiness.sh` case each fail on main cd8cab5e and pass with the fix.

answers.constraints: cmd_change lessons: a text next action and a JSON next action are two projections of one value; the Archive script's sentences are kept in step with pull_request_archive_sentence; REQ-change-129/REQ-cmd-change-029 (#889): an archive HEAD already contains is the reopen path and is not refused; when Git cannot answer, upstream_archive_of returns None and every other gate applies.
